clue.text: One who endorses roasting absurd play's conclusion

indicators.note: absurd means senseless, so the letters of roasting are put into a nonsensical new order
the conclusion of the play is its final letter

explanation.surface: A critic gives a glowing endorsement while roasting the ending of a ridiculous play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' rearranges ROASTING into SIGNATOR, and 'conclusion' takes the Y ending play's.
explanation.definitionFit: A signatory puts their name to a document, thereby formally endorsing or agreeing to it.

clue.text: Current rules reversed about greeting that's heard in Kenya

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed rules wrap round the greeting
reversed means the word for rules is read backwards

parts.note: rules are laws
hi is a casual greeting
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Local rules on how to greet people, as you would hear them spoken in Kenya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' gives SWAL, and 'about' wraps it round the greeting. 'Current' leads the clue but its I goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is the national language spoken across Kenya, so it is what you hear there.

clue.text: Heave goods around area

indicators.note: around means the goods letters surround the area letter

parts.note: G stands for good, so goods are two Gs

explanation.surface: An instruction to lift merchandise around a warehouse floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to retch, the throat heaving as if about to vomit.

clue.text: Are current lines and numbers entered first?

parts.note: AC is alternating current
an ode is a poem, i.e. some lines of verse

explanation.surface: A question about whether electrical cables and figures come first in some installation.
explanation.definitionFit: An area code is the prefix of digits dialled before the local phone number.

clue.text: Swimmer's more fashionable without a top

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter of the word is removed, as this is a down clue

parts.note: hotter means more in vogue

explanation.surface: A swimmer looks more stylish without a top on.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a river mammal noted for its swimming.

clue.text: At last stubbly nurse got reconditioned shaver

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of stubbly
reconditioned means rebuilt, so the letters of nurse got are put together anew

explanation.surface: A stubbly patient finally has a nurse who got hold of a refurbished electric razor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconditioned' rearranges NURSEGOT into OUNGSTER after the Y from 'At last'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young shaver is an old-fashioned informal term for a boy or youngster.

clue.text: Pity about Europe wasting its money, some in India

indicators.note: about means round, so the pity word goes around the remaining letters

parts.note: rue means regret or pity

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the currency is removed from Europe

parts.note: the euro is Europe's currency

explanation.surface: Regret that Europe squanders its funds, some of which go to India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' leaves PE once the currency goes; 'about' wraps the pity word round it. 'some in India' means some money there, following on from 'money'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India, so some Indian money is rupees.

clue.text: Withdraw actual line about to be introduced

indicators.note: to be introduced means put inside, so the about letter goes into actual

parts.note: real means actual
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: An instruction to retract a factual statement that was about to be put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something, such as a faulty product or a statement, is to withdraw it.

clue.text: Mark is not quite on time getting into ground

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: punctual means on time

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mark, nearly late, arrives at the ground just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims PUNCTUAL to PUNCTUA; 'ground' rearranges INTO as TION. 'Mark' looks like a name; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark is a symbol such as a comma; punctuation is the collective term for such marks.

clue.text: Rely on foul saving time for wing

indicators.note: saving means keeping or holding, so the scrambled letters hold the time letter
foul means corrupt or mess up, so the letters of rely are jumbled

explanation.surface: Depend on a foul shot buying time for a winger on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' rearranges RELY as ELYR, and 'saving' holds T inside it to give ELYTR.
explanation.definitionFit: An elytron is the hardened forewing of a beetle, a wing case.

clue.text: Get bigger people to stand in for us during month

indicators.note: to stand in for means to replace, so people take the place of us

parts.note: August is a month
men are people

explanation.surface: Increase the staff so that others can deputise for us during a busy month.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to increase or make larger, a synonym for growing bigger.

clue.text: Creepy posh governess nurses cold

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: nurses means holds close, so the cold letter sits inside

parts.note: a nanny is a children's governess or nurse
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An unsettling upper-class governess looks after someone with a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny means eerie and strange, the same unsettling quality as something creepy.

clue.text: Like columns to be representative, not conservative

indicators.note: not means without, so the conservative letter is taken out

parts.note: iconic means typical or representative of something

explanation.surface: Pillars meant to symbolise something, but not in a Conservative style.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture, describing a style of column.

clue.text: Curious type using hooter when leaving car?

definitions.meaning: a nosy parker is a busybody who pries into others' affairs
read whimsically, a ... parks by the nose, hooter being slang for nose

explanation.definitionFit: A busybody is a prying, inquisitive person, the sense of curious type.

clue.text: Go off with a gun, returning for timepiece

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to rot is to go off or decay
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: Someone runs off with a gun and comes back in exchange for a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator is a precision clock used as a standard for setting other timekeepers.

clue.text: Thoroughly popular team dismissed

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a side is a team
out means dismissed, as in cricket

explanation.surface: A well-liked team was completely bowled out.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something inside out is to know it completely and in detail.

clue.text: Primate, old, managed grand university function

parts.note: ran means managed
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
tan is the trigonometric function tangent

explanation.surface: An old primate organised a lavish university event.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape, and apes are primates.

clue.text: Deep source of power, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a poetic name for the open sea, the deep
a principal supply line, as for gas or electricity

explanation.definitionFit: Main as a noun means both the high sea and a principal utility pipe or cable.

clue.text: Reportedly, what our energy bill is based on?

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the clue words are pronounced

parts.note: these two words spoken together resemble the unit

explanation.surface: A householder asks what their electricity bill is actually calculated from.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity is billed in units of watt-hours, so the charge is calculated on them.

clue.text: Steer round extremely nasty stone

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the steer letters go around the rest

parts.note: an ox is a steer, a castrated bull

indicators.note: extremely points to the two end letters of nasty

explanation.surface: Guide a vehicle around a very unpleasant rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Where to cultivate fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A gardening question about where to grow fruit or vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot planted with fruit trees.

clue.text: Crashed on a safari in two races?

indicators.note: crashed means wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A vehicle crashed during a safari while competing in a pair of rallies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashed' rearranges ONASAFARI. 'races' looks like motor races; it means ethnic groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Afro-Asian describes people or things of both African and Asian descent.

clue.text: Boy comes up on track, not taking a breather

indicators.note: comes up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: not taking means leaving out, so the letter a is dropped

parts.note: a trail is a track

explanation.surface: A boy races on along a track without pausing for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns SON into NOS; 'not taking' drops A from TRAIL to leave TRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is a nasal opening through which one breathes.

clue.text: Just receiving training in public

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the training letters go inside

parts.note: only means just
PE is physical education, training at school

explanation.surface: Someone is only getting coaching out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly means doing it publicly, without concealment.

clue.text: What malingerer has picked up that's in his cellar?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: a malingerer fakes illness, so has a sham pain

explanation.surface: Asking what a shirker caught, as if it were stored in his wine cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: A malingerer has a 'sham pain'; said aloud it sounds like the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling wine, the sort of thing laid down in a cellar.

clue.text: Record traveller's memory

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a Rom is a Romany, a traveller

explanation.surface: A record that a traveller remembers.
explanation.definitionFit: EPROM is erasable programmable read-only memory, a kind of computer memory chip.

clue.text: African port barrels India imported

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so the India letter goes inside

parts.note: tuns are large casks or barrels
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An African harbour takes in barrels shipped from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia, a Mediterranean seaport in North Africa.

clue.text: Flower an officer's put around Hollywood citizen

indicators.note: put around means wrapped round, so the officer letters enclose the citizen

parts.note: Lt is a lieutenant, an officer
Citizen Kane is the classic Hollywood film

explanation.surface: A flower placed by an officer around a Hollywood resident.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkanet is a plant of the borage family with blue flowers.

clue.text: Part-time judge has clubs stolen? Send for more

indicators.note: stolen means taken away, so the clubs letter is removed

parts.note: a recorder is a part-time judge in the English courts
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A judge's golf clubs are stolen, so he orders replacements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests golf; it is the card suit C.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder is to place another order, requesting a further supply.

clue.text: Cheat Charlie Houseman for one

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fraudster named Charlie Houseman.
explanation.walkthrough: A houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseman is a junior hospital doctor, one example of a doctor.

clue.text: The German Times? It's a classic

parts.note: der is a German word for the
by means times, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A newspaper query about a German edition of The Times being a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is one of the five British flat-racing Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby at Epsom is one of the classic horse races of the English flat season.

clue.text: Heath left after miners, indicating figures

indicators.note: after means placed behind, so the left letter follows

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers
erica is the botanical name for heath or heather

explanation.surface: Ted Heath departed after the miners' strike, as the figures showed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' suggests Edward Heath, the 1970s Prime Minister who fell after a miners' strike; here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerical means expressed in numbers, that is, relating to figures.
